newsitem.title: COMOROS: Ruling party wins majority in Comoran elections.
newsitem.headline: Ruling party wins majority in Comoran elections.

text.p: The ruling party in the Comoro Islands won a parliamentary majority on Monday in first results from Sunday's general elections but one Islamist opposition leader said the voting was rigged.

The main opposition alliance, the Forum for National Recovery, boycotted the elections, saying it wanted elections for a constituent assembly, a revision of electoral registers and a new independent electoral commission.

Two prominent opposition figures were arrested on the eve of voting but the authorities released them on Monday and public prosecutor Mohamed Abdelouahab told Reuters they would not face charges in connection with arson attacks on polling stations.

The ruling National Rally for Development won 26 of the first 32 seats won outright in the 43-seat federal assembly. Independents won two seats and the Islamist National Front for Justice (NFJ) won two, official sources said.
Final results from the first round of voting should be ready on Monday night, they added. In cases where no candidates wins more than half the vote, people will vote again next Sunday.
Candidate Ahmed Abdullah Sambi, Iranian-trained leader of the NFJ, said on Monday he objected to the conduct of voting.
"In some polling stations our representatives were not allowed in while in others the ballot boxes were not opened before the starting of voting," he told Reuters.
"If the government attempts to cheat us by validating the contentious polling stations and making the ruling party win, we will have to draw adequate lessons," he added.
Sambi will be a candidate in second-round voting in Mitsamiouli, the second largest town on Grande Comore island.
Government radio said the turnout in the elections in the former French colony was high but observers said on Sunday it was low.

The opposition leaders -- former prime minister Mohamed Abdou Madi and the leader of the Democratic Front party, Mustapha Said Cheikh -- had been held for questioning since Saturday after the prefecture, the main administrative building in the capital Moroni, was burned down.
Last Thursday the offices of the governor of Moheli island were burned down, destroying electoral materials stored there.
No one has claimed responsibility for these and other apparent arson attacks in the last few days.
